Definition: from G3164; a battle, i.e. (figuratively) controversy:--fighting, strive, striving.
BiblicalUsage: Mache is fighting, contention, strife, and the New Testament treats it as something to flee rather than to win. 2 Corinthians 7:5 says Paul had fightings without and fears within, and James 4:1 asks where wars and fightings come from and answers: from lusts that war in our members. 2 Timothy 2:23 and Titus 3:9 both say to avoid the foolish questions that gender strifes.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe James 4:1 names the root of every quarrel I have ever been in: the fight outside starts as a war inside. My position is that the apostles are right to tell me to avoid the argument rather than win it, because a strife I refuse to enter cannot master me.
